$comment: Hand-curated. Marks a benchmark signal (same-model gap or near-band criterion) as explained or tracked so docs/BENCHMARKS.md shows it as known rather than open. `case` and `metric` are fnmatch patterns; `metric` may be a list of them. `explained` needs the mechanism and evidence in `ref`; `tracked` needs an open issue. See tools/benchmarks/benchmarks.py and #54.

entries.note: The hand-written Flow deck omits ROCK (pressure +3.6 %, GOR -15 % alone); from a deck generated by the engine's own setup ResSim agrees to 0.15 / 0.53 / 0.80 %.

The hand-written deck samples SGOF at ten nodes, overstating krg by up to 41 % around the initial Sg; JutulDarcy reads the same deck. From a generated deck ResSim agrees with Flow to 0.09 % cumulative oil, 0.24 % GOR.
JutulDarcy and Flow on the same hand deck differ in oil rate during the steep first 20 days; time-step resolution suspected, not shown.
FIM (sparse, dense) gas production vs Flow on generated decks while oil agrees exactly; PVT table-edge conventions (#35) suspected, not shown.
The plain deck's sub-day TSTEPs are where flowexp_comp cut extra steps, so the matched-timestep comparison is only approximate there; the skin variant, without them, agrees to 0.0074 bar.
The absolute grid error (~2.7e-4 at nx 20 to 40) is unchanged; the physical PVT table liberates less gas, so the relative gap rose while the contraction ratio stayed ~0.54.
Same source compiled for two targets; the 1e-9 band is a floating-point courtesy, not a tolerance budget. The measured ~1e-12 is the expected size.

Gas rate spreads across all three simulators on the PVT-risk decks (FIM between JutulDarcy and Flow), while oil agrees exactly: consistent with differing PVT table-edge conventions (#35), not yet shown.
FIM's end-of-run oil rate differs from JutulDarcy while JutulDarcy and Flow agree; cumulative oil agrees with Flow to 0.05 %.
